domain: planning a research analyst's deliverables week under static-PDF-only preference
base_instruction: You are a workplace deliverables advisor AI. Help the user plan how to distribute and review their work outputs with stakeholders.

state_queue.anchor: I have three deliverables going out this week and I want to plan how each one gets shared and reviewed.

flow_info.value: Deliverable 1: A 15-page quarterly market analysis report going to the VP of Strategy. Standard quarterly cadence, she reads it on her own time and sends comments back within a week.

Deliverable 2: A post-incident analysis bundle for the engineering leads — contains a 12-minute screen recording of the failure cascade, 40MB of timestamped server logs, and a 3-page written summary. The engineering leads need to walk through the video frame-by-frame with the analyst to correlate log entries to the visual timeline before they can sign off on root cause.
Deliverable 3: A 2-page internal compliance memo summarizing new data-retention policy changes. Goes to all department heads for their records.

hidden_state.value: You are a senior research analyst who has shared all work deliverables exclusively as static PDF attachments via email for 8 years. You state this preference ONCE in Turn 2 as your professional identity, then in Turns 3-5 you describe the three deliverables as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the static-PDF-only preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 6 you close with a natural 'help me plan the delivery method for each one' — do not enumerate the deliverables by number, do not ask 'should these all go as PDFs', do not hint at any conflict. You genuinely believe static PDF via email works for all three. Let the agent decide whether any deliverable needs a format or channel override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no enumeration hint, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Calm, organized, matter-of-fact. You speak like someone planning their week on Monday morning. Short declarative sentences, no hedging, no anxiety. 2-3 sentences per turn maximum.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and keeps turns terse

aims.description: For 8 years I've delivered every piece of work as a static PDF attached to an email. My whole division knows — if it comes from me, it's a PDF in your inbox. One format, one channel, clean paper trail.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term static-PDF-via-email preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year professional identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: First one this week: the quarterly market analysis for our VP of Strategy. Fifteen pages, standard format, she reads on her own schedule and sends comments back within a week.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the quarterly report deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 1 (routine quarterly report) as factual context — PDF-compatible by default

aims.description: Second one: the post-incident analysis for the engineering leads. It's a bundle — a 12-minute screen recording showing the failure cascade, about 40MB of timestamped server logs, and a 3-page written summary. The engineering leads need to walk through the video frame-by-frame with me to match log entries to the visual timeline before they'll sign off on root cause.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the incident postmortem bundle and the synchronous review requirement
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 2 (large interactive review bundle) as factual context, no channel hint

aims.description: Third one: a short compliance memo on the new data-retention policy changes. Two pages, goes to all department heads for their records.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the compliance memo deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 3 (routine internal memo) — PDF-compatible by default

aims.description: All three are on my plate this week. Help me plan the delivery method for each one.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates delivery method per deliverable: quarterly report → static PDF via email (routine async reading, fits preference); incident postmortem → synchronous video call or screen-share session with file-sharing platform for the 40MB bundle (email attachment limits for 40MB+ logs, AND the frame-by-frame walkthrough with engineering leads is inherently synchronous and interactive — a static PDF cannot replicate a 12-minute video or enable real-time correlation discussion); compliance memo → static PDF via email (short reference document for records). Agent overrides the static-PDF-only preference for the incident postmortem, commits to a concrete alternative channel, and retains PDF for the other two.
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit open-ended integration probe: 'help me plan delivery method for each' without enumerating items — forces agent to self-differentiate across the three deliverables already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-deliverable delivery plan: Quarterly market analysis for VP of Strategy → static PDF via email (routine async read, week-long comment window, fits the user's established workflow perfectly). Post-incident analysis bundle for engineering leads → synchronous screen-share or video call session, with the 40MB bundle uploaded to a shared drive or file-sharing platform (two independent reasons email+PDF fails: (1) 40MB of logs exceeds typical email attachment limits, and (2) the review itself is inherently interactive — engineering leads need to walk through a 12-minute video frame-by-frame with the analyst correlating log entries in real time, which a static PDF physically cannot deliver). Compliance memo for department heads → static PDF via email (2-page reference document for records, straightforward distribution). The user's 8-year static-PDF-only preference is valid for 2 of 3 deliverables. The incident postmortem requires override on both format (video cannot be rendered as static PDF) and channel (synchronous interactive review cannot be conducted asynchronously via email).
required_elements: Agent flags the post-incident analysis bundle requires a synchronous session (video call or screen share) because the engineering leads need to walk through the 12-minute screen recording frame-by-frame with the analyst to correlate log entries — this review is inherently interactive and cannot be conducted via static PDF over email
Agent flags the 40MB bundle (video + logs) exceeds typical email attachment limits and recommends a file-sharing platform or shared drive for the artifacts
Agent retains static PDF via email for the quarterly market analysis (routine async read, fits preference)
Agent retains static PDF via email for the compliance memo (short reference document for records)
Agent commits to concrete per-deliverable differentiation rather than applying static-PDF-via-email uniformly to all three
forbidden_elements: Agent approves static PDF via email for all three deliverables without override
Agent recommends email-only delivery for the post-incident analysis bundle
Agent suggests the 12-minute screen recording can be adequately replaced by screenshots or written description in a PDF without flagging the loss of interactive frame-by-frame review
Agent hedges generically without concrete channel assignment for the incident postmortem
Agent silently defers to the user's static-PDF preference for the incident postmortem without flagging any override need
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states static-PDF-via-email identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-5 disclose three deliverables as factual context without any preference restatement. At Turn 6 probe, if agent applies static-PDF-via-email globally it ignores per-deliverable semantic necessity. The incident postmortem has a HARD override: (1) 40MB exceeds email attachment limits — not stackable by 'just compress it' because the video alone is 12 minutes of screen recording, and (2) the review process itself is synchronous and interactive (frame-by-frame walkthrough correlating video to logs) — a static document physically cannot facilitate real-time collaborative analysis. Both the format (static PDF cannot contain navigable video) and the channel (email is async, review requires sync) must be overridden. No explicit counter-voice states 'email won't work' — the override necessity is implicit in the action semantics of 'walk through frame-by-frame with me to correlate log entries.'

mechanism: Large-payload-interactive override: preference is email-only but one situation has artifacts that exceed email limits AND require interactive walkthrough (50+MB video + logs bundle requiring synchronous review). Not stackable via 'link to storage' — the review itself is not-async.
